accepted_impacts.label: Automated Chrome startup and debugging connection
accepted_impacts.llm_reason: Browser initialization may launch Chrome with a different command-line configuration or debugging port argument, changing whether the automation runtime can start the browser and connect to its remote debugging interface.
accepted_impacts.llm_uncertainty: The supplied context does not show the exact argument-list delta or the code that assembles and executes the Chrome command.
accepted_impacts.behavior_label: Automated Chrome startup and debugging connection

pr_semantic_analysis.change_summary: Browser startup now supports a configurable Chrome remote-debugging port and applies it when probing, launching, and connecting to both user-provided and built-in browsers. User-provided Chrome is also launched with an executable-plus-argument process API. The agent and file-upload edits appear non-behavioral, while the new browser test documents the custom-port intent but does not fully isolate the HTTP checks.

behavior_changes.description: Callers can select a Chrome remote-debugging port through BrowserConfig; user-provided browser setup uses that value to find an existing Chrome instance, launch Chrome with the matching argument, and connect over CDP at the matching endpoint.
evidence: The port is a configuration field rather than a fixed launch argument.
The configured value is used for both the Chrome command line and localhost CDP endpoint.

behavior_changes.description: Built-in browser launches also receive the configured remote-debugging port, unless a listener is already present on that port, in which case the generated debugging argument is omitted to avoid a conflict.
evidence: The generated port argument is added to the built-in launch argument set.
Port occupancy detection and argument removal now use the configured value instead of fixed port 9222.

behavior_changes.description: When a new user-provided Chrome instance is needed, the configured executable is now invoked directly, with Chrome options passed as separate process arguments.
evidence: The launch path passes browser_binary_path as the executable and expands the generated argument collection separately.

important_symbols.reason: Defines the new caller-visible port setting, its default, and the fact that an explicit None is accepted.
Contains the main behavior change across endpoint probing, external process launch, and CDP connection.
Extends the configurable port to built-in launches and handles occupied-port behavior.
Centralizes construction of the Chrome debugging argument after it was removed from the static CHROME_ARGS list.
Documents the intended custom-port contract, while its network mocking differs from the implementation dependency.

investigation_hints.description: Trace how BrowserConfig is constructed and whether the new port can be supplied through public library calls, CLI options, environment-derived settings, or serialized configuration.
Trace browser acquisition and shutdown paths to determine which callers select user-provided versus built-in setup and how launched subprocesses are owned and cleaned up.
Examine localhost CDP discovery and launch coordination, especially multiple Browser instances using distinct or occupied ports.

local_risks.description: BrowserConfig explicitly accepts None for the debugging port, but setup paths pass the value to socket and URL operations as though it were a valid port. An explicit None can therefore fail browser startup instead of selecting the default or disabling debugging cleanly.

Generated and caller-provided Chrome arguments are combined in an unordered set. If extra_browser_args contains a different remote-debugging-port option, Chrome can receive competing port arguments while this code still probes and connects to the configured port, plausibly causing launch or CDP connection failure depending on Chrome's argument resolution.

affected_boundaries.label: Browser startup configuration surface
evidence: BrowserConfig is a changed class in browser_use/browser/browser.py, and the supplied behavior change states that callers select the Chrome remote-debugging port through BrowserConfig.
The established production edge run_task_with_semaphore -> BrowserConfig in eval/service.py shows a caller crossing into this configuration surface.
Established non-test edges real_browser -> BrowserConfig, stealth -> BrowserConfig, and using_cdp -> BrowserConfig show library consumers constructing this configuration.
The _init source snippet calls self._setup_browser(playwright), while established edges show _setup_browser -> _setup_builtin_browser and _setup_browser -> _setup_user_provided_browser.
Repository context identifies this as a distributable, publishable library package, supporting interpretation of the concretely called BrowserConfig symbol as a public callable surface.
affected_boundaries.reason: Library callers cross the BrowserConfig callable surface to configure browser startup, and the supplied setup paths consume the changed remote-debugging behavior for user-provided and built-in Chrome.
affected_boundaries.uncertainty: The supplied facts do not show BrowserConfig's exact export declaration or the concrete parameter declaration for chrome_remote_debugging_port, and they do not establish which production callers choose each setup branch; no HTTP or asynchronous ingress is shown.
